batch_strategy: Measure connected ratio curves and loading contrasts around recent failures, with related scaffolds that distinguish endpoint-specific corrections from transferable structure-condition relationships. Favor missing condition regions over further interpolation in recently well-predicted regions. Use supplied point predictions as frozen references; single-predictor quantile widths receive little weight because they are not calibrated epistemic uncertainty.

choices.reason: Ethyl cinnamate at 20/1, 50 uL tests loading transfer of the newly measured modest weak-eluent response. The 100 uL labels 0baeb34a1650e9409f2a and e6dcf9d6f65fa598a38e measured 6.33/19.26 and 9.59/28.68 mL. The new 7.10/18.57 prediction tests whether the corrected curve transfers to lower loading.

Ethyl p-methoxybenzoate at 2/1, 50 uL begins a fixed-loading moderate-ratio pair. Its 8.42/21.53 prediction suggests substantial completion already at 2/1, informed by high-loading observation 0637945ca309d8122e64. An independent loading tests whether that early broad response is reproducible.

Pair the same ester at 5/1, 50 uL. Predicted completion falls from 21.53 mL at the selected 2/1 condition to 17.14 mL here. Measurement distinguishes a supported local response from interpolation influenced by the high-loading 2/1 record and the 100 uL 5/1 label b324251a07260af49364.

Add ethyl p-methoxybenzoate at 20/1, 50 uL, predicted 14.08/29.96 mL. Recent high-loading 6d54149d618f026681ef measured 11.14/30.00, with onset overpredicted at acquisition. This tests whether completion transfers across loading while onset changes, connecting to low-loading 50/1 observation 810b16f35a3a86f451ce.

tert-Butyl acetoacetate at 2/1, 50 uL tests an early-ratio loading boundary after 0af9d219be9872711215 exposed excessive predicted 20/1 growth. Compare the 4.43/8.10 prediction with high-loading 2/1 record ac6cfe67adcb860efabf and low-loading 5/1 anchor b008f92639d8bb738954 to distinguish an early transition error from weak-eluent curvature.

Ethyl acetoacetate at 20/1, 150 uL completes loading transfer from ac81adfab5ec8ce768db and 3b400f57f8dcc4cdbd83. Its 25.70/60.88 prediction provides a useful contrast to the much shorter measured tert-butyl ester at this ratio and loading. This constrains ester-substituent and loading interactions.

The alpha-benzyl acetoacetate at 50/1, 150 uL completes a loading series with 2b97a1e0a6a4b944b760 and 61771d230b285babe4b6. Their onsets decrease from 56.96 to 49.93 mL while completion stays near 98 mL. The 51.08/93.93 prediction tests endpoint-specific continuation to higher loading.

Methyl mandelate at 10/1, 150 uL tests loading transfer from d8fcb58722028dbf9c02 at 50 uL, 44.43/60.99 mL. The prediction is 41.90/59.59. This donor-containing ester supplies a chemically meaningful contrast to the neutral aromatic esters without assuming that all ester loading responses coincide.

p-Fluoroacetophenone at 20/1, 100 uL connects same-loading 10/1 and 50/1 observations 7fdf49a091a855c0138f and c53b8c93f8ee1304dfd0. Its 15.31/31.94 prediction tests intermediate curvature and compares with high-loading 20/1 anchor bed2f1430d0964e86fcb after weak-eluent underprediction.

p-Iodoacetophenone at 50/1, 50 uL tests loading transfer of recent 93d0b949ca6dc0685979, which measured 22.49/47.60 mL at 150 uL. The new prediction is 22.15/48.87. This establishes whether the repaired weak-eluent response generalizes across loading rather than remaining a single-condition correction.

p-Bromoacetophenone at 5/1, 100 uL fills the earlier part of its same-loading curve between 4ed02da322b210a5f98f and 2420964caf34a1de2a5d. Recent 605436d35600502e8c2e exposed substantial 50/1 underprediction. This 8.26/15.96 prediction tests whether the discrepancy is confined to later ratio growth.

2,6-Difluorobenzaldehyde at 5/1, 150 uL starts a matched moderate-ratio extension of its high-loading curve. Compare with low-loading 37b8d0f56019b0d4fad3 and high-loading weak-eluent anchors 7d5a5e7ce28dafd856c2 and 0e5b806832eaea6e01b6. This locates loading effects before the measured 20/1 onset mismatch.

Complete the difluoroaldehyde extension at 10/1, 150 uL, predicted 9.43/22.77 mL. Together with the selected 5/1 condition and measured 20/1 result 7d5a5e7ce28dafd856c2 at 14.39/26.71, it tests where onset growth and completion growth diverge.

The methylenedioxy acetophenone m39 at 2/1, 150 uL begins a connected curve between measured 1/1 record 3c4c856ec5ee29c66540 and 20/1 record a6a0404c3ad65c6d9326. The 11.66/27.81 prediction tests whether appreciable growth develops immediately beyond the strong-eluent anchor.

Measure m39 at 5/1 and the same 150 uL loading. Its 20.18/40.44 prediction implies substantial growth beyond the selected 2/1 point. This fills a missing relationship for an oxygen-substituted aryl ketone, allowing comparison with the selected p-methoxyacetophenone condition.

Add m39 at 10/1, 150 uL, predicted 23.56/44.70 mL. The selected 2/1 and 5/1 points and measured 20/1 anchor a6a0404c3ad65c6d9326 distinguish early growth, a plateau, and renewed later growth. A connected curve should teach more than another isolated weak-eluent endpoint.

p-Methoxyacetophenone at 5/1, 100 uL tests the predicted 11.33/24.93 response. Current 10/1 predictions are lower, and measured 5f2fc9606fb31b009ccc gives 7.60/20.15 there. With 2/1 anchor f2931e18ce0362f7a6c0, this label tests whether the intermediate-ratio hump is supported.

p-Methoxybenzaldehyde at 1/1, 150 uL directly tests a remaining predicted completion hump: 18.01 mL here versus measured 12.63 mL at 2/1 in 4e7e45a513ce579c5ce3. Recent pure-EA 9ef318afb1f6bac186ff measured only 8.48 mL completion. This discriminates local curvature from unsupported interpolation.

1-Phenylethanol at 2/1, 50 uL establishes the first point of an independent loading-specific ratio comparison. The prediction is 10.19/21.64 mL. At 100 uL, f559a4634c60d81f5f15 has later onset than the weaker-eluent 10/1 record 859ae738b615cf17b849; the new pair tests transfer of that unusual shape.

Pair 1-phenylethanol at 10/1, 50 uL with its selected 2/1 condition. The 6.07/17.28 prediction carries a decrease in both endpoints despite weaker eluent. This tests whether the unusual 100 uL curve is reproducible at another loading, following the failure of an analogous cross-loading reversal hypothesis for m117.

1-Phenylpropanol at 5/1, 150 uL fills the gap between acutely earlier 2/1 observation 56f8cdbb3999b366d947 and the later 10/1 and 20/1 regime. Its 8.55/18.29 prediction tests a missing transition in a close benzylic-alcohol comparison to 1-phenylethanol.

Measure 1-phenylpropanol at 20/1, 150 uL. Low- and middle-loading records 2cf4f6424b85ab121943 and c627405cf70a0daacc94 measured onsets of 42.23 and 34.61 mL with similar completion. The 37.81/59.99 prediction tests whether higher-loading onset continues decreasing or follows a different relationship.

m-Bromobenzyl alcohol at 2/1, 50 uL begins a loading pair before its discrepant 5/1 records. At 5/1, 4e5ead91320bd24d485e measured 21.18/34.03 mL, while the 100 uL result ec6846c0fcb7df17c97d was much shorter. This 7.41/13.73 prediction locates the earlier boundary.

Pair m-bromobenzyl alcohol at 2/1, 100 uL. Its prediction is nearly identical to the selected 50 uL point, despite the large measured 5/1 contrast in 4e5ead91320bd24d485e and ec6846c0fcb7df17c97d. The pair tests whether that contrast is already present under stronger eluent or localized near 5/1.

Dibenzylamine at 10/1, 150 uL tests loading transfer of 70cba7a21b5a01fb8e73 at 100 uL, 46.67/78.07 mL. The prediction is 46.52/79.78. This checks the delayed regime independently; the early 5/1 record d5234e966aa231be05e5 uses another loading and alone cannot isolate the solvent transition.

p-Aminoacetophenone under pure EA at 100 uL supplies a missing strong-eluent baseline, predicted 6.00/12.39 mL. The 1/1 low-loading record 762190c8d9f5b2d1a89a and 2/1 records 183af335033005f96b97 and 9fcf89b00bb880c8a5ba show much later endpoints. This tests where that response begins.

Pair p-aminoacetophenone at 1/1, 100 uL with its selected pure-EA baseline. The 11.51/23.23 prediction tests the strong-eluent transition and loading transfer from 762190c8d9f5b2d1a89a. It helps determine whether recent 2/1 underprediction reflects an earlier transition or later curve growth.

Diethylaminoethyl acrylate at 2/1, 50 uL completes loading coverage with 304fb0fdb486ae4b7a07 and recent 906bd247e050658f99d8. Their completion volumes were 32.81 and 35.04 mL while onset decreased. The 14.68/33.73 prediction tests whether this endpoint-specific pattern extends to low loading.

Measure the same tertiary aminoester at 1/1, 150 uL. Observations a595d5f1882c39914392 and 9a60cb4735780275034e showed decreasing onset but nearly unchanged completion from 50 to 100 uL. This 13.65/25.37 prediction completes the earlier-ratio loading contrast and separates it from the 2/1 completion response.

The formally charged P/O structure at 1/1, 50 uL begins a loading contrast around recent middle-loading 87a651fc86ed976bd374. Compare with low-loading 2/1 record c6e28d5262ab7fb32107. This tests whether an onset-loading association already exists under strong eluent without transferring the exceptional 10/1 contrast globally.

Complete the P/O 1/1 pair at 150 uL. Predictions at 50 and 150 uL are nearly identical, about 6.15/11.97 mL, while measured 2/1 onsets differ across loading in c6e28d5262ab7fb32107 and 942c95c0b3a64c876639. The pair identifies the ratio boundary of any loading association; solution speciation is unknown.

2-Bromopropionic acid at 5/1, 150 uL tests whether the marked onset-loading decrease measured at 20/1 in b24f66ff77974f8ba6e1 and 53a9a2469f8d4ead8732 already develops earlier. Compare its 11.22/20.44 prediction with low-loading 5cc67d02b8fad1c648d6. The invalid-looking 50/1 middle-loading interval is not treated as a mechanism.

hypotheses.content: Ester solvent-response curves depend on carbonyl connectivity and neighboring groups. Recent cinnamate labels show substantially less weak-eluent growth than predicted at acquisition; p-methoxybenzoate completion grows while its onset was overpredicted; tert-butyl acetoacetate reaches its delayed regime later than its acquisition prediction implied. Transfer of these relationships across loading remains incompletely tested.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Several common ester environments have different conditional slopes. Loading contrasts and early-ratio anchors can prevent a correction learned for one ester from spreading to other connectivities or to both endpoints indiscriminately.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the corrected aromatic-ester curves transfer to low loading, and do the ethyl acetoacetate, alpha-benzyl acetoacetate, and mandelate loading extensions retain distinct endpoint responses?

hypotheses.content: Recent para-halogenated acetophenone labels support substantial weak-eluent retention that was underestimated for the bromo and iodo compounds. Their observed 50/1 onsets are more similar than their acquisition predictions suggested, although loading conditions and loading solvents differ. Difluoroaldehyde results additionally require endpoint-specific conditioning rather than one shared carbonyl correction.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Intermediate-ratio and loading-transfer labels can determine where recent corrections belong. This should improve local structural transfer among aromatic carbonyls without imposing a universal halogen effect.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Are the newly repaired weak-eluent ketone responses supported at intermediate ratios and another loading, and where does the difluoroaldehyde high-loading curve develop between 5/1 and 20/1?

hypotheses.content: Current intermediate-ratio predictions for oxygen-substituted aryl carbonyls contain unresolved response shapes. m39 is predicted to grow substantially before 10/1, whereas p-methoxyacetophenone and p-methoxybenzaldehyde have predicted completion humps relative to neighboring conditions. Additional oxygen functionality is a chemical reason to investigate these differences, not evidence that the predicted humps are real.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Connected curves distinguish structural effects on transition location from model interpolation artifacts. The comparison spans ketone versus aldehyde and methoxy versus methylenedioxy environments.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does the m39 high-loading curve follow the predicted early growth and plateau, and are the m115 5/1 and m118 1/1 completion humps supported by measurement?

hypotheses.content: Donor-containing scaffolds require separate endpoint- and loading-conditioned response curves. The unusual measured 1-phenylethanol curve at 100 uL and the short m-bromobenzyl-alcohol 5/1 result at 100 uL should not be generalized across loading without independent contrasts. 1-Phenylpropanol provides a related scaffold with a substantially growing weak-eluent response.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Independent loading-specific comparisons can reveal whether unusual curves represent local catalog behavior or transferable relationships. Related alcohols help prevent a generic donor correction from obscuring distinct onset and completion regimes.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does low-loading 1-phenylethanol retain the 2/1-to-10/1 decrease, does the bromobenzyl-alcohol loading contrast exist already at 2/1, and how does higher-loading phenylpropanol enter its delayed regime?

hypotheses.content: Nitrogen-containing scaffolds exhibit different endpoint-specific loading associations. Recent p-aminoacetophenone 2/1 labels have similar completion across low and high loading, while the tertiary aminoester has earlier high-loading onset and later completion. The phenylpyridine 2/1 and methylquinoline loading midpoint were comparatively well predicted, limiting the case for another broad nitrogen-associated adjustment.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Strong-eluent boundaries and matched loading extensions can teach when an onset association changes into a completion association. This tests transfer between aniline, tertiary amine, secondary amine, and heteroaromatic environments without assuming identical silica interactions.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Where does p-aminoacetophenone's delayed response begin, do the tertiary aminoester loading patterns persist at 1/1 and 2/1, and does dibenzylamine's measured 10/1 regime transfer to 150 uL?

hypotheses.content: The P/O scaffold's extreme 10/1 loading contrast may be localized and does not justify a global formal-charge retention offset. Its measured 2/1 loading contrast chiefly affects onset, while recent 1/1 middle-loading completion is modest. Whether the onset-loading association is already present at 1/1 remains unresolved.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The paired strong-eluent labels constrain the ratio boundary of a difficult loading interaction. They can reduce inappropriate propagation from extreme records, while the absent speciation information limits mechanistic interpretation.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At 1/1, do low and high loading differ primarily in onset, in both endpoints, or little at all?

hypotheses.content: The m117 onset reversal from 10/1 to 20/1 is a reproducible solvent-response shape across sample loadings.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The independent 150 uL pair shows increasing onset and completion, rejecting cross-loading generalization of the exceptional 100 uL curve. The reversed interval at the original 10/1 record further limits mechanistic interpretation. This supports testing unusual predicted shapes independently before extending them to neighboring rows.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the remaining unusual shapes in 1-phenylethanol and p-methoxybenzaldehyde survive the selected independent condition comparisons?

feedback_interpretation:
The latest ester outcomes changed the priority from generic weak-eluent growth to connectivity-specific curvature and loading transfer. Ethyl cinnamate measured only 9.59/28.68 mL at 50/1, against its acquisition prediction of 24.57/47.97. tert-Butyl acetoacetate was close at 10/1 but measured 16.94/39.22 at 20/1, well below its acquisition prediction. For p-methoxybenzoate, completion at 10/1 and 20/1 was comparatively accurate while onset was too late. Benzoylacetate's new 20/1 and 50/1 completion remained near 18 mL, supporting its modest response; I therefore avoid spending more labels densely interpolating that repaired curve.

The m117 150 uL pair measured 8.48/25.33 at 10/1 and 13.51/37.01 at 20/1. This rejects the proposed cross-loading onset reversal. I retain that contradiction as a warning against propagating an exceptional record, and test other unusual response shapes with independent comparisons. The new p-methoxybenzaldehyde pure-EA and 2/1 labels also expose a useful unresolved boundary for its currently predicted 1/1 completion.

All three para-halogenated acetophenones had substantial measured 50/1 retention. The bromo and iodo results were especially underpredicted at acquisition, weakening confidence in the previously different predicted response shapes. Difluoroaldehyde's high-loading 20/1 onset was underestimated while completion was close; its 50/1 completion was overestimated. I consequently use intermediate-ratio labels rather than assuming a shared offset for both endpoints.

The m125 pure-EA 300 uL DCM baseline transferred reasonably from 50 to 150 uL sample loading, so it receives no further midpoint label. Cinnamic acid, however, measured completion of 50.30 mL with 2000 uL DCM under pure EA versus 31.91 mL in the 1500 uL record; this weakens transfer of loading-solvent-volume insensitivity across ratios and scaffolds. The small recorded density difference remains part of that comparison. The selected bromopropionic-acid condition addresses an available loading boundary without claiming to test the cinnamic-acid volume effect directly.

Salicylaldehyde's latest loading extension and the oxime's strong-eluent extension were comparatively accurate, reducing their priority. Phenylpyridine at 2/1 and the methylquinoline loading midpoint were also close to acquisition predictions. In contrast, p-aminoacetophenone and the tertiary aminoester retained useful endpoint-specific discrepancies, motivating earlier-ratio and loading-boundary measurements. These are historical acquisition errors, not assumed residuals of the current predictor.
batch_rationale:
The batch combines recent failure repair with experiments that identify where corrections should apply. Aromatic esters receive a low-loading ratio curve and weak-eluent transfer points; beta-ketoester and hydroxyester extensions test whether loading effects depend on connectivity and donor functionality. The halogenated carbonyl choices connect recently surprising weak-eluent labels to intermediate ratios or another loading. Their value lies in discriminating response shapes, not in selecting large retention volumes.

Three m39 conditions form a connected curve at fixed loading between measured strong- and weak-eluent anchors. The m115 and m118 additions test specific intermediate-ratio humps. Independent alcohol curves examine whether unusual measured patterns transfer across loading, with phenylpropanol supplying a close structural comparison. Nitrogen-containing scaffolds receive missing strong-eluent boundaries and loading contrasts, while the P/O pair localizes a difficult interaction without treating formal charge as a complete mechanistic explanation.

Across the pool, many predictions change very little with loading, although measured loading associations vary by molecule, ratio, and endpoint. The selected contrasts directly test that model behavior. I avoid selecting multiple IDs with the same molecule-condition tuple within this batch and reduce effort in regions recently measured accurately. Exploration concerns missing condition relationships among represented molecules rather than molecular novelty. Learning these conditional relationships should improve V1 and V2 generalization across catalog rows while limiting inappropriate transfer from isolated anomalous labels. No unrecorded concentration, pH, flow, or column variable is assumed.
